task.name: No producer validates the issue body it writes, so forge files and edits issues its own gate refuses
task.story_text:
---
depends_on:
  - issue-2725
---

## Problem

Components that write issue bodies do not validate what they write, so forge routinely files
and edits issues its own gate refuses. Two instances are filed — the post-run hook files
findings with no type label (#2713), and `forge diagnose` appends a section whose citations
trip the plan-in-body check on non-bug issues (#2136) — but neither owns the invariant, and
the surfaces that have not yet been observed failing are not covered by either.

## What

One invariant, enforced across every producer: a component that writes an issue body renders
through the shared specification and validates the result before mutating anything. A
component that cannot produce a conforming body fails visibly rather than filing an object
its own gate will refuse.

Covers `forge shape`, `forge groom`, `forge diagnose`, `forge report`, `forge todo`, the
post-run hook, and any surface added later.

## Why

Slice 5 of the typed-intake-contract epic. The two filed instances are leaves of one defect:
nothing requires a producer to check its own output. Fixing them individually leaves the
invariant unowned and the remaining producers untested, which is how the second instance
arrived a month after the first.

Producers that legitimately write non-admissible objects — `forge todo`, an unresolved
`forge shape`, a cause-unknown diagnosis, the post-run hook's untriaged findings — are not
exceptions to the invariant. They declare the state they intend, and the check is that the
rendered object matches it.

## Acceptance criteria

- Every component that creates or edits an issue body declares the lifecycle state it
  intends the result to occupy, and validates the rendered body through the shared
  evaluation before the mutation is made.
- The rendered body is structurally conforming for the state its producer declared, and the
  shared evaluation's result matches that declaration. A producer that intends a draft may
  write a non-admissible object; what it may not do is write one whose evaluated state
  differs from the state it declared.
- An unexpected refusal prevents the mutation rather than being written and discovered
  later.
- A producer that cannot render a conforming body reports that it cannot, naming what it
  could not satisfy, rather than writing a body that will be refused.
- A producer that edits an existing body does not make an admissible body inadmissible; where
  its addition would do so, it reports rather than writes.
- Producer conformance is covered by tests enumerating the producers, so a newly added
  producer that skips validation fails the suite rather than being discovered in the corpus.

## Example

The failure this closes, observed while filing issues for this epic:

```
$ forge diagnose --issue 2690      # lands a Diagnosis section carrying file:line citations
$ forge groom 2690
  blocking  implementation_plan_in_body   ... 1 file:line reference(s)
```

One forge command produced a body a second forge command refused, and neither declared what
state it intended the result to be in.

handoff.summary: Added src/theforge/shape_check/producer.py — a stdlib-only shared boundary holding a closed registry of every issue-body producer plus validate_issue_body/compare_declaration/require_conforming_body, which evaluate a rendered title/body/labels through the existing shape_check.check and compare the resulting ShapeVerdict to the state the producer declared. Two declaration modes: strict equality for authoring producers (forge-report-create, forge-report-update, forge-todo-create, forge-advisory-finding, post-run-hook-finding, forge-intake-autofix) and delta-scoped for editing producers (forge-shape, forge-groom, forge-diagnose, forge-todo-triage, forge-intake-reopen-context), where an edit conforms if it matches the declaration or introduces no new refusal code and does not turn an admissible body inadmissible. Wired every create/edit seam through it before mutation: cmd_shape's _apply_to_github, run_groom's edit/file write, diagnose_flow._land_artifact's body_section branch, cmd_report's create and publication-state update (judged against the target repo's own gate verdict via compare_declaration), _create_todo and _triage_todo's editor path, advisory_conventions._maybe_file_issue, remediation._remediate_one's edit-mode write, and remediate_shape_gate_skip. Both shell hooks and the generated hook template now validate each finding body through the module's CLI over stdin, fail closed on any nonzero exit (mismatch, missing interpreter, theforge not importable), resolve an interpreter from the installed forge executable with FORGE_PYTHON to override, and carry the bug type label. Conformance is guarded by per-producer refusal tests at each mutation seam plus a static scan of src/theforge/**/*.py and .forge/hooks/*.sh, tolerant of both shell-command and Python argv-list spellings, that fails when a mutation seam appears which no registered producer accounts for.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Every component that creates or edits an issue body declares the lifecycle state it intends the result to occupy, and validates the rendered body through the shared evaluation before the mutation is made.
acceptance_criteria.notes: All 11 producers declare and validate before their mutation seam. PRODUCERS is a closed registry — an unregistered producer raises rather than validating. forge report declares against the target repository's gate verdict rather than this checkout's, preserving the cross-repo contract established by evaluate_target_gate.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The rendered body is structurally conforming for the state its producer declared, and the shared evaluation's result matches that declaration. A producer that intends a draft may write a non-admissible object; what it may not do is write one whose evaluated state differs from the state it declared.
acceptance_criteria.notes: forge todo declares ShapeVerdict.NEEDS_TYPE as a pinned literal (verified: todo:draft alone yields needs_type), the post-run hook declares NEEDS_OPERATOR_ACTION, and a cause-unknown diagnosis declares DIAGNOSIS_CAUSE_UNKNOWN — all deliberately non-admissible, all checked for equality. Declarations are computed from producer intent (proposal classification, Diagnosis fields, artifact.partial) rather than by re-reading the rendered body, so they are falsifiable rather than self-fulfilling.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: An unexpected refusal prevents the mutation rather than being written and discovered later.
acceptance_criteria.notes: Each seam is covered by a test asserting the mocked mutation (_apply_to_github, edit_issue_body, _gh_edit_body, _create_issue/_update_body, todo gh issue create and body edit, hook gh issue create, remediation edit_body) is not called on refusal.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A producer that cannot render a conforming body reports that it cannot, naming what it could not satisfy, rather than writing a body that will be refused.
acceptance_criteria.notes: ProducerValidation.report() names the producer, declared vs evaluated verdict, any newly introduced refusal codes, and every reason code with its detail. forge shape additionally refuses outright when a classification has no declarable state for a body restructure, rather than writing something unvalidatable.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A producer that edits an existing body does not make an admissible body inadmissible; where its addition would do so, it reports rather than writes.
acceptance_criteria.notes: Enforced by the regressed_from_runnable and new_refusal_codes rules whenever previous_body is supplied. This is what closes #2136 — a Diagnosis section with file:line citations landed into an enhancement is now refused, which required inverting test_explicit_body_section_override_still_writes_non_bug_issue_body since it asserted the defective behavior.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Producer conformance is covered by tests enumerating the producers, so a newly added producer that skips validation fails the suite rather than being discovered in the corpus.
acceptance_criteria.notes: tests/test_issue_body_producer_conformance.py enumerates producers three ways: PRODUCERS must equal the union of APPROVED_SEAMS, each approved file must name its producer id, and the static scan must find no mutation seam outside the approved set. A non-vacuity assertion fails loudly if the matcher stops matching, addressing the plan reviewer's concern that a literal-substring scan would pass empty against Python argv lists.

story_deviations: The plan's producer list omitted three current producers with unvalidated mutation seams — advisory_conventions._maybe_file_issue, remediation._remediate_one, and remediate_shape_gate_skip. The static guard in Step 6 would have found them and failed the suite, so all three were registered and wired (forge-advisory-finding, forge-intake-autofix, forge-intake-reopen-context). This matches the plan reviewer's P1 note.

The plan had editing producers declare a single exact verdict. Measured against the real gate, that produced false refusals: groom legitimately lands on non-runnable verdicts (_next_command has a branch for exactly that), and diagnose would have refused good diagnoses over pre-existing unrelated defects in the operator's body. Editing producers therefore declare a state but are judged on the delta they introduce. Strict equality is retained where the invariant is load-bearing — groom's cause-unknown bug cannot become runnable.
forge shape validates only when there is a real body delta. A no-op write asserts nothing new, and the label-only path does not touch the body.
Hooks pass the body on stdin rather than via a temp file. mktemp was blocked in this environment, and the temp file bought nothing.

The plan accepted 'theforge not importable' as a carried risk. Left as-is, validation was silently disabled in the very environment the tests run in, so the hooks now resolve an interpreter from the installed forge executable's shebang before falling back to PATH.

Three existing tests were updated because they encoded behavior this story overturns or fixtures that predate it: test_explicit_body_section_override_still_writes_non_bug_issue_body (inverted — it asserted #2136), two diagnose fixtures given the bug label they always implied, the todo triage gh issue view field list (now title,body,labels — labels are needed to evaluate), and one report assertion switched to call_args_list[0] since the publication rewrite is now gated separately.

They exercise scripts/cut-rc.sh and sprint/lock.py, neither touched here, and fail identically before these changes. make dev-check exits nonzero because of them.

handoff.summary: Iteration 1 addresses the single P1: the shared producer boundary permitted a declared-state mismatch for editing producers. The strict/non-strict split in shape_check.producer.compare_declaration is removed entirely. A declaration is now one of two forms, both matched exactly: a concrete ShapeVerdict (or set), where the evaluated verdict must equal a declared state regardless of what caused a difference — including a refusal the producer did not introduce; or PRESERVE (declared=None), meaning 'unchanged, or improved by clearing', for a producer scaffolding into a body it does not own. PRESERVE is compared over blocking findings rather than over the verdict, because the verdict alone answers neither question: it can hold still while a defect is added underneath a higher-precedence finding, and it can legitimately move when an open Diagnosis section trades blocking needs_diagnosis for advisory diagnosis_cause_unknown. Both forms additionally refuse a regression from an admissible body. verdict.refusal_codes became verdict.blocking_codes to match, since lifecycle-refusal codes must not count as introduced defects. Producer call sites already used concrete or PRESERVE declarations, so only groom needed its comment corrected to explain why PRESERVE rather than RUNNABLE is its honest claim; the strict=True kwarg was dropped from report, todo, advisory, remediation and groom, and the --strict flag from the CLI plus both hooks and the hook template (their behavior is unchanged — they always required exact matching).

ac_verification.criterion: Producer conformance is covered by tests enumerating the producers, so a newly added producer that skips validation fails the suite rather than being discovered in the corpus.
ac_verification.evidence: tests/test_issue_body_producer_conformance.py:36 enumerates approved mutation seams, tests/test_issue_body_producer_conformance.py:75 fails on unapproved body mutation seams, tests/test_issue_body_producer_conformance.py:97 requires each approved seam to name its producer, and tests/test_issue_body_producer_conformance.py:106 requires the registry and approved seam list to match.; Implemented in tests/test_issue_body_producer_conformance.py under TestStaticSeamScan, which does a regex scan of src/theforge and hooks, matching against APPROVED_SEAMS and registered PRODUCERS.; tests/test_issue_body_producer_conformance.py guards conformance three ways: (1) PRODUCERS registry equals union of APPROVED_SEAMS producers (line 114, TestStaticSeamScan::test_every_registered_producer_owns_a_seam); (2) static scan finds all mutation seams gh issue create|edit with --body(-file)?, normalizes shell and Python spellings by stripping quotes/brackets (lines 31–34), fails if seams exist unaccounted in APPROVED_SEAMS (line 96–106); (3) each approved seam file is verified to name its producer (line 108–115). Non-vacuity check: scan is not broken when matcher stops matching (line 75–81 asserts found files >= APPROVED_SEAMS count). Scanner resilient to multiline and argv spellings via 400-char lookahead and whitespace normalization (lines 31, 43). Per-producer tests enumerate refusal at each seam: 9 test classes each validate the specific producer and mutation (e.g., test_create_validates_before_gh_runs, test_the_declared_state_check_gates_the_edit_seam).

plan_review.findings:
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Step 6's producer registry is incomplete. src/theforge/advisory_conventions.py:_maybe_file_issue creates task-shaped issues, while src/theforge/intake/remediation.py:_remediate_one and remediate_shape_gate_skip edit issue bodies through _default_edit_body. The latter reopen-remediation path does not run shape_check on new_body before edit_body. These are current producers, not hypothetical future surfaces. The proposed static scan would find their gh mutation seam, but no plan step, file list, producer id, or test routes them through the contract, so the suite cannot pass while satisfying the all-producers acceptance criterion.
  Suggestion: Add producer ids and validate-before-mutate wiring for advisory issue filing, sprint intake auto-fix, and shape-gate-skip remediation; include src/theforge/advisory_conventions.py, src/theforge/intake/remediation.py, tests/test_advisory_conventions.py, and the remediation test suites in the plan.
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] The shell-hook importability risk remains carried: Steps 1 and 4 rely on invoking a Python module, while the mitigation explicitly accepts environments where theforge is not importable. That preserves fail-closed behavior but can disable conforming post-run findings in generated downstream hooks.
  Suggestion: Expose validation through a reliably available forge CLI command or invoke the interpreter associated with the installed forge executable, and exercise a generated hook end-to-end in a representative installed environment.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Carried risk 3 (shell hooks may run where theforge is not importable). Step 4 says validation failure must be visible and non-filing, but it does not state what happens when the *validator itself* cannot run (ImportError / missing interpreter) as opposed to returning a mismatch verdict. The generated hook template ships to repos whose environment forge does not control, so an ambiguous branch here silently reverts the post-run hook to the pre-fix unvalidated behavior it is supposed to close (#2713).
  Suggestion: Make the hook fail-closed explicitly: a nonzero exit from the validator for ANY reason (mismatch, ImportError, interpreter missing) skips the gh issue create and prints the reason to stderr. Add a generated-hook test in Step 5 covering the validator-unavailable branch, not just the verdict-mismatch branch.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 6's static scan is described as looking for gh issue create/gh issue edit with --body/--body-file, which matches the shell hooks but not the Python call sites, where the argv is a list — e.g. src/theforge/cli/todo.py:209 builds ['gh', 'issue', 'edit', issue_number, '--body-file', str(temp_path)] and _create_todo builds a multi-line list containing 'create'. A literal-substring scan would report zero Python producers and the guard would pass vacuously.
  Suggestion: Have the scan match both forms — a token-level or regex match tolerant of list-literal quoting/newlines across src/theforge/**/*.py and .forge/hooks/*.sh — and assert the scan finds a nonzero, expected count of call sites so a broken matcher fails loudly instead of passing empty.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 3's declaration for forge todo create — 'the declared draft verdict produced by the shared gate' — is circular: a declaration defined as whatever the gate returns can never mismatch, which defeats the AC. _create_todo (src/theforge/cli/todo.py:65-84) passes only todo:draft with no type label, so check_missing_type fires and the verdict is NEEDS_TYPE.
  Suggestion: Pin the declaration to the literal ShapeVerdict.NEEDS_TYPE (or whichever verdict the todo:draft label set actually produces once confirmed) so a future change to todo's label set trips the mismatch instead of being absorbed.
- [P1-impl] [google-gemini-3.5-flash-api] When shell hooks execute, the local Python environment might not have theforge dependencies installed. Hook validation should detect when theforge cannot be imported and report a clear diagnostic rather than failing with raw import errors.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules

Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
